en: In the language of India: *Ārya-jayamati-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*. In the language of Tibet: *’Phags pa rgyal ba’i blo gros zhes bya ba theg pa chen po’i mdo* (The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Victor’s Intelligence"). Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great saṅgha of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks.
Thus have I heard at one time: the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great saṅgha of bhikṣus and a vast multitude of bodhisattvas.
There, the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattva Jayamati:
Then the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattva Jayamati:
"O Jayamati, a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family who desires merit should make offerings to the Tathāgatas.
O Jayamati, a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family desiring merit should worship the Tathāgatas.
One who desires wisdom should apply oneself to learning;
one who desires wealth should increase generosity.
It must be increased; indeed,
one should observe the precepts out of a desire for higher realms— note this reversal from the Tibetan.
One who seeks heaven should guard ethical discipline;
one who desires wealth should cultivate generosity;
one who seeks beauty should cultivate patience.
One who desires a beautiful form should cultivate patience.
One who desires eloquence should show reverence toward the gurus. One who desires eloquence should honor the teachers.
One who desires dhāraṇīs should be free from manifest pride;
one who seeks happiness should completely avoid all evil deeds.
These should be avoided; indeed,
one who desires primordial wisdom should abide in correct mental engagement (*yoniśo-manasikāra*).
One who desires liberation should abandon all evil.
One who seeks meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) should cultivate thorough mental attention (*yoniśomanasikāra*) extensively.
One who desires the happiness of all sentient beings should generate the mind set on awakening;
one who wishes to bring about the well-being of all sentient beings should generate the mind set on awakening.
One who desires a melodious voice should cultivate truthful speech;
one who desires a pleasant voice should speak the truth.
One who desires qualities should delight in solitude. One who seeks the Dharma should attend upon spiritual friends;
they should be attended upon.
One who desires the Dharma should rely upon a spiritual friend.
One who desires calm abiding (*śamatha*) should frequently practice non-association; one who desires calm abiding should remain mostly free from worldly bustle.
One who desires insight (vipaśyanā) should cultivate the frequent analytical observation of emptiness;
one who desires higher vision (lhag mthong) should repeatedly examine phenomena as empty.
One who desires the world of Brahmā should cultivate loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
One who seeks the excellence of gods and humans should undertake the ten paths of wholesome action.

Desiring the perfect abundance of the enjoyments of gods and humans, one should correctly adopt and abide in the ten paths of virtuous action. Desiring complete nirvāṇa, one should take great delight in the phenomena of emptiness.
"One who desires all virtuous qualities should worship the Three Jewels;
one who wishes to attain every excellence should make offerings to the Triple Gem.

The Blessed One spoke thus, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Jayamati, being uplifted in mind, as well as those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly—including gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

When the Blessed One had spoken these words, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Jayamati, along with that entire assembly and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had said.
The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Questions of Jayamati" is completed.
The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Questions of Jayamati" is finished.
